questions.stem: What type of ion does magnesium form, and why?

options.text: Mg- because it gains one electron
Mg2+ because it loses two outer electrons
Mg+ because it loses one outer electron
Mg2- because it gains two electrons

questions.explanation: Magnesium has the electron configuration 2,8,2. It loses its 2 outer electrons to achieve the stable configuration 2,8 (like neon). Losing 2 electrons gives it a 2+ charge, forming the Mg2+ ion.

questions.stem: What is the formula of potassium sulfide?
questions.explanation: Potassium forms K+ ions (charge +1) and sulfur forms S2- ions (charge -2). To balance the charges, you need 2 potassium ions for every sulfide ion: 2(+1) + (-2) = 0. The formula is K2S.
